newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemalan leader fires top two military officials.
newsitem.headline: Guatemalan leader fires top two military officials.

text.p: President Alvaro Arzu fired Guatemala's top two military officials on Friday, in a move human rights observers called a defeat for reform elements in the powerful armed forces.

Defence Minister Gen. Julio Balconi and the head of the elite Presidential Guard, Gen. Hector Camargo, were both fired just six months after they helped the government negotiate a peace treaty ending 36 years of civil war with leftist insurgents.

"Generals Julio Balconi, minister of defence, and Hector Camargo, chief of the presidential guard, have not adapted to the new requirements needed by the government over the next few years," government spokesman Ricardo de la Torre told reporters.
The two generals were known as moderates within the country's influential military.

Gen. Hector Barrios took over as the new defence chief and Gen. Marco Tulio Espinoza as chief of staff. Barrios is seen as a hardliner within the army, which is widely accused of human rights violations during the civil war, when an estimated 100,000 people were killed and another 40,000 disappeared.
The moves took some observers by surprise, because changes in the military have normally been announced on June 30, Army Day. On Monday Arzu had announced only minor changes in the army's command.
Human rights groups criticised the move as giving sway to hardliners within the army, which agreed to cut its forces sharply as part of the Dec. 29, 1996 peace accords.
"They are paying the price now for having achieved what they did during the peace agreement," Mario Polanco of the Mutual Support Group said.
De la Torre said the decision had been planned for some time and responded to the army's new peacetime role.
